title: A Brahmin Appeals to the Khalsa Against a Tyrant Sayyad

blocks.text: A new narrative opens by praising the Khalsa as a power that can act where courts and governors refuse justice. The aggrieved father explains that There is a town known as Luhari Jalalabad near Delhi, where a tyrannical Sayyad has abducted his daughter and terrorized the surrounding people.

The page frames his appeal as a test of Khalsa responsibility toward the weak. No official will confront the offender, so the Brahmin comes to the Sikh camp convinced that the Panth alone still acts in the cause of protection and benefaction.

Warnings immediately arise about distance, danger, and the Sayyad's influence near Delhi, yet the moral pressure of the plea is stronger than caution. The episode therefore begins not with conquest but with a rescue mission grounded in justice.
